main_text.p: communicationes: cum suo ipsius testimonio eum ad quem scribimus convincimus. Nono,&χαί[?] vota atq; precationes, quibus mętem[?] iis ad quos scribimus, meliorem precamur. Decimò, integritatis & candoris professiones: cùm vt noftra, & natura, & amicitia postulat, liberè nos atq; aperte agere oftendimus. Postremò [illegible, ~6 letters] pollicitationes ac delationes, amoris, studij, officij, quæ posita in fine, paulò asperius atq; acerbius dicta, leniunt atq; mitigant.Collocatio ex postulatoriarum epistolarum. Collocatio autem ita in huius generis epistolis instituitur: vt in exordio fit: vel querela & obiurgatio ex abrupto facta. lib.3.epist.6.lib.5.epist.1. Vel occasionis & causarum instituté scriptionis expositio. lib.5.epist.5.7.li.7.epist.23. Pars altera propositio ipsam μέμψιν[?] obiurgationem atq; expostulationem continet. lib.5.epist.5.7. Tertia eiusdem rationes, cùm docentes tùm amplificantes completatur, petitas à contentione atq; comparatione acceptorum & neglectorum officium. lib.3.epist.6. lib. 5. epist. 5. Factis & meritis præclaris. lib.3.epist.6.lib.5. epist.1.5.7. personę cui iniuria infertur dignitate. lib.3.epist.6. lib.5. epist.1. pollicitationibus multis atque magnis. lib.3.epist.6. Testi-

page.notes: Greek words after "Nono," and after "Postremò" are doubtful; the Greek after "Postremò" is illegible. The word after "mętem" is doubtful. "μέμψιν" is a tentative reading. The printed "vt" has been corrected to "ut" in the Latin: the transcription keeps "vt" as printed in the text, per the u/v rule it should read "ut" (see text). The marginal note is a running note in italics that spans four lines; its breaks were joined without hyphens because none were printed.
